newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Electrolux says cuts in Europe, North America.
newsitem.headline: Electrolux says cuts in Europe, North America.

text.p: Swedish household appliance group Electrolux said its 2.5 billion crown restructuring programme meant operational cuts mainly in Europe and North America.
It also said it would continue its existing product line.
"The closures will mainly concern Europe and North America," chief executive Michael Treschow told a news conference.
He said the company had too many plants manufacturing the same things.
The company said earlier that its restructuring programme included closing about 25 of 150 plants and cutting 12,000 staff from a workforce of 105,000 over the next two years.
"These plans mean we will continue with the products and product lines we have today," he said. "It's about merging operations."
It is, however, too early to say which units will be closed, he said.
"The management will this month present precise proposals," he said.
The 2.5 billion crowns of restructuring costs will be recovered over two years, Treschow said.
"We have said that we will see through the programme over a two-year period," he said. "We must save this money (2.5 billion crowns) during that time."
Total savings would clearly be larger he said, declining to specify further.
"You don't have to be a genius to see that savings must be larger than expenses for us to be able to reach our margin targets," he said.
The company's long-term financial targets include an operating margin of 6.5 -7.0 percent and a return on equity of 15 percent. Electrolux plans to meet these targets in 2000.
